meta.label: Alpha Centauri
meta.title: Alpha Centauri
meta.blurb: A triple-star system just over four light-years away — the closest stars to our Sun.

meta.label: TRAPPIST-1
meta.title: TRAPPIST-1
meta.blurb: A single ultracool dwarf circled by seven Earth-size planets, 39 light-years away.

meta.label: Sirius
meta.title: Sirius
meta.blurb: The most brilliant star in our night sky — a hot blue-white sun with a dense white-dwarf companion, 8.6 light-years away.

meta.label: Kepler-90
meta.title: Kepler-90
meta.blurb: A Sun-like star with eight known planets — the first system found to rival our own, 2,840 light-years away in Draco.

featured.title: Kepler-90
featured.tagline: A rival to our Solar System

meta.label: Kepler-186
meta.title: Kepler-186
meta.blurb: A red-dwarf system 580 light-years away — home to Kepler-186f, the first Earth-size world found orbiting in the habitable zone.

meta.label: K2-18
meta.title: K2-18
meta.blurb: A red dwarf 124 light-years away, circled by K2-18 b — a sub-Neptune in the habitable zone and one of our best hopes for a world with water.

meta.label: 55 Cancri
meta.title: 55 Cancri
meta.blurb: A naked-eye double star 41 light-years away with five known planets — among them 55 Cancri e, a super-Earth drowned in an ocean of magma.

meta.label: Barnard's Star
meta.title: Barnard's Star
meta.blurb: The closest single star to the Sun — an ancient red dwarf racing across our sky, with four sub-Earth worlds packed into a single week.

featured.title: Barnard's Star
featured.tagline: The fastest star in our sky

meta.label: Wolf 359
meta.title: Wolf 359
meta.blurb: A red dwarf in the tail of Leo, 7.86 light-years away — one of the smallest stars known, too faint for the eye, and restless enough to flare several times a day.

featured.title: Wolf 359
featured.tagline: One of the smallest stars known
